cards.text: A father is teaching his son, and he's just said the LORD founded the earth by wisdom (Prov 3:19). Now he leans in: "My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment." That's dad for HOLD ON TO THIS, I'm not saying it twice.

cards.question: The father tells his son to hold on to sound judgment and discernment. What does he say they'll be to his son's soul?

cards.text: He also calls them "adornment to your neck," so sound judgment is jewelry now. FINALLY, a necklace that still shows up under a mustache like mine.

cards.question: With sound judgment and discernment, the father says his son's foot will still stumble now and then.
The father keeps going. When his son lies down, what does the father promise?

cards.text: And when he rests, his sleep will be sweet. Friend, I spent YEARS lying awake in the back of a junk drawer, so this one hits me right in the handle.
Then the father says, "Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked," and he has a reason ready.

cards.question: The father tells his son not to fear sudden danger. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD will be his confidence
He will see it coming early
He is strong enough to face it

cards.text: The LORD will also "keep your foot from the snare." Then the father turns from his son's safety to how his son treats the people around him.

cards.question: The father tells his son not to withhold ___ from the deserving when it's within his power to act.
The father says it's fine to tell your neighbor to come back tomorrow, even when you already have the means to help today.

cards.text: "Come back tomorrow" when the help is already sitting RIGHT THERE? That's hitting the snooze button on your neighbor, and the father says NOPE.

cards.question: The father tells his son not to devise evil against his neighbor. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He trusts you and lives beside you
He might find out what you did
He could pay you back for it

cards.question: The father adds that his son shouldn't accuse a man without ___ when that man has done him no harm.

cards.text: Then the father points to a different kind of man: a violent one. I bet a guy like that struts around like he's WINNING, while I once lost an argument to the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with.

cards.question: The father tells his son not to choose any of the violent man's ways. What else does he tell his son not to do?
The father explains that the LORD detests the perverse but is a friend to the upright.

cards.text: Now the father lines things up in pairs, like two cookies side by side on a tray. "The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous."

cards.question: Next pair: the LORD mocks the mockers. In the other half of that pair, who does He give grace to?
The last pair: the wise will inherit ___, but fools are held up to ___.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Life' is the only positive option. 'A heavy load' and 'A hard lesson' are both negative. A father urging his son to hold on to something would not promise either, so the right answer stands out by tone. It is also much shorter than the two wrong answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions. The violent man is strutting like he's winning, and Papa Dorin once lost an argument to the batteries. Both are about winning and losing, but the comparison doesn't share the core action, so a stranger would say 'huh?' about how the two connect.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin losing an argument to the dead batteries is a new event in the junk drawer. The backstory only says the batteries argued with each other over who had the most charge left. Made-up small moments are allowed around his bakery, not added to his drawer history.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
